walkthroughs.body_html:
Programming Fundamentals — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Programming Fundamentals brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Programming Fundamentals.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which is a high-level programming language?
options: Assembly
Machine code
Python
Binary
Internet Data Engine
Integrated Development Environment
Internal Debugging Editor
Interpreted Dynamic Executable

mcqs.q: What does an INNER JOIN return?
options: Only rows with matching values in both tables.
All rows from both tables combined.
Writing code that does not work.
Only the inner columns of each table.

mcqs.q: What does inheritance allow a subclass to do?
options: Only the inner columns of each table.
Replace the superclass entirely.
Copy code from any unrelated class.
Reuse and extend the attributes and methods of its superclass.

mcqs.q: What is abstraction in computer science?
options: Writing code that does not work.
Making something abstract art or vague.
Only the inner columns of each table.
Removing unnecessary detail to focus on essential features of a problem.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “IDE”?
options: Assembly or machine code, closer to hardware, providing direct control of the processor.
Set of rules defining valid combinations of symbols and keywords in a programming language.
Integrated Development Environment: editor, compiler/interpreter, debugger and tools combined in one application.
Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.

Non-executing text in source code that explains the program to human readers.
